governance.note: nyiso-43 (winter spread + Algonquin ceiling + oil-attribution basis fix) PLUS tranche_startup_amortization - the ISO-NE Order-825 fast-start pricing analogue already in the codebase (v2 scope: fast-start-capable CT_PEAKER/CT_CHP econ tranches + CT/CC quick-response peak bands carry the NREL start cost, amortized into P1 bids by each tranche's own P0 run lengths). NYISO's real market runs the same structure (GT hybrid / fast-start pricing lets peaker commitment costs set LBMP), so the lever is real structure with a measured cost basis and no residual input. PROBE FINDING: it moves CT_PEAKER only 4.90 -> 4.75 TWh (2024; actual 2.13) because with the de-leaked neutral econ bands the P0 base-cost pass runs the CTs in long blocks, so the per-MWh amortized start cost is small - the lever is worth keeping but CANNOT substitute for the missing NYISO CT offer-level grounding (the 0c6c833 de-leak's documented open root cause). C1-2024 ST_GAS -3.35 TWh therefore still FAILs (MODEL MISS - not ledgerable: the actual is sound; the model lacks the CT commitment/offer-level structure). C2-2025 gas -0.1%, C5a -2.6/-5.4/-3.8% all PASS as in nyiso-43; C3a -15.4/-14.9/-13.0 and C3b 0.207/0.201/0.195 improve slightly on 43 (the amortized commitment cost is honest price content).

_open_items: (0) BLOCKING, repo-level: the NYISO CT_PEAKER/CT_CHP offer-level grounding left open by commit 0c6c833 (Kill cross-ISO leakage of ERCOT-fitted gas offer bands). With neutral 1.0 econ bands the LI/NYC peakers (Bayonne, Barrett GTs, Glenwood, Equus, Edgewood, Freeport) over-run ~2.5x actual and displace ST_GAS below the C1 band - EVERY NYISO solve on current main fails C1-2024, including a re-solve of the keeper-41 config itself (verified: CT 4.69/ST 7.65). Grounded closure candidates, none satisfiable from data on disk today: (a) LI/NYC peaker delivered-fuel basis (LDC citygate / interruptible service premium; kerosene for the dual-listed frames) - no measured series on disk; (b) a NYISO-specific offer markup - the 2024 SOM confirms offers sit ABOVE bid-based reference levels ('output gap ... due to low reference levels rather than inappropriately high offers') but publishes no per-class markup; (c) DEC Peaker Rule NOx run-hour limits (regulatory, forward-valid) - not on disk; (d) fast-start amortization (this probe) - real but insufficient alone. The CEMS marginal-HR route is ruled out (run-28 lesson: CT marginal HR is 0.66-0.85x base, BELOW neutral). (1) DATA-BLOCKED eastern-NY winter hub level (licensed Iroquois Z2 series ask; Dec-2024/Dec-2025 winter levels are allocation-funded only). (2) The ledgered reserve-scarcity / offer-markup frontier (AS data on disk is prices, not condition-varying requirements). (3) Upstate shoulder collapse behind the measured CE TTC: per-interface external flows/ratings data ask (see nyiso-43 SUMMARY E1 decomposition).
